articleBlocks: Fence, Hedge, and Wall first made me think about barriers in general, which felt close but still too loose.
Moat kept that idea alive for a moment because it is also something that keeps one space separate from another.
But Boundary line changed the board.
That clue does not just describe a barrier. It describes a property limit.
Once that legal land-reading showed up, Fence, Hedge, Wall, and even Moat all started behaving like ways to separate one property or protected set of grounds from another.
The answer was Things that separate properties.
Looking back, the puzzle is tricky because most of the clues can live inside a vague 'barriers' bucket until one clue makes the real frame much narrower.
fullAnalysis: Fence, Hedge, and Wall first made me think about barriers in general, which felt close but still too loose.
Moat kept that idea alive for a moment because it is also something that keeps one space separate from another.
Boundary line was the clue that changed the solve. That phrase does not sound like a random obstacle; it sounds like property law.
Once the board moved into a property-reading, Fence, Hedge, and Wall all became much cleaner because each one can divide one person's land from another person's land.
Moat then stopped feeling like a weird medieval outlier and started reading as a boundary around protected grounds or an estate.
The answer was Things that separate properties.
What makes this board hard is that 'barriers' feels nearly right. Boundary line is what forces the more precise answer.
solutionNarrative: Fence, Hedge, and Wall gave me a broad barrier read right away, and Moat did not immediately break it. That first path felt plausible because every clue did involve separation in some physical sense.

The board became solvable when Boundary line arrived. That clue pulled the whole set away from generic protection or obstruction and into a property-specific frame. After that, Fence, Hedge, Wall, and even Moat all read like ways land or grounds can be marked off from neighboring space.
